title: "Audit 10: lung histology as a confounder of lung contrasts"
author: "Jannik Franken"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
---

## Purpose

The 85 lung lines used in models are of several histologies: adenocarcinoma,
squamous cell carcinoma, small cell lung cancer and others. Driver mutations
differ between histologies (e.g. KRAS mostly in adenocarcinoma), and so may
metabolism. A lung genotype contrast that ignores histology may then partly
compare histologies. This notebook checks how histology relates to the
genotypes, to batch and to the metabolic profiles, and how adding histology
to the lung models changes their results.

**Decision supported:** whether histology enters the lung contrasts as a
blocking factor (catalogue families F2, F3, F5), and whether histology
contrasts (F1) are feasible.

## Inputs

- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds`
- `data/raw/cancer-cell-lines/depmap_24Q4/Model.csv` (Oncotree subtype; local only)
- `data/derived/cancer-cell-lines/shorthouse_v1/02_cell_lines.tsv` (Cellosaurus disease text, for comparison)
- `config.yml`: `contrast`, `differential.contrasts`

## Methods

Histology was taken from the DepMap Oncotree subtype and grouped into
adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, neuroendocrine (small cell lung
cancer and carcinoid), other non-small cell (large cell, adenosquamous,
mucoepidermoid, not otherwise specified) and other (mesothelioma,
SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumour). The association of each genotype
with histology was tested with Fisher's exact test (simulated p-value), and
that of batch with histology likewise. The metabolic effect of histology was
measured as the R² of histology on the leading principal components and with
a limma F-test of histology in `~ batch + histology`. The lung contrasts were
refitted with histology added to the design, and their results compared with
the current ones.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/use_case.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/plotting.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/mutations.R"))
source(here::here("analyses/cancer-cell-lines/R/differential.R"))
config <- load_config()
raw_dir <- uc_dir(config, "raw")
derived_dir <- uc_dir(config, "derived")
output_dir <- uc_dir(config, "output", "audit_10_lung_histology")
set.seed(config$contrast$seed)

data <- readRDS(file.path(derived_dir, "shorthouse_analysis_v1.rds"))
```

## 1. Histology of the lung lines

```{r histology}
models <- readr::read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, config$depmap$dir, "Model.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE,
                          col_select = c(ModelID, OncotreePrimaryDisease, OncotreeSubtype))
cellosaurus <- readr::read_tsv(file.path(derived_dir, "02_cell_lines.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    select(line, disease_cellosaurus)

# Oncotree subtype grouped into five histologies
lung <- data$lines %>%
    filter(in_models, tissue == "Lung") %>%
    select(line, tissue, batch, ModelID) %>%
    left_join(models, by = "ModelID") %>%
    left_join(cellosaurus, by = "line") %>%
    mutate(histology = case_when(
        OncotreeSubtype == "Lung Adenocarcinoma" ~ "Adenocarcinoma",
        OncotreeSubtype == "Lung Squamous Cell Carcinoma" ~ "Squamous",
        OncotreePrimaryDisease == "Lung Neuroendocrine Tumor" ~ "Neuroendocrine",
        OncotreePrimaryDisease == "Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer" ~ "Other NSCLC",
        TRUE ~ "Other"
    ))
count(lung, histology, OncotreeSubtype, sort = TRUE)

# Cellosaurus disease text next to the grouping, for a plausibility check
lung %>% count(histology, disease_cellosaurus) %>% arrange(histology, desc(n)) %>%
    preview_table(caption = "Histology group vs Cellosaurus disease")
```

## 2. Histology, genotypes and batch

```{r genotypes}
genes <- c("KRAS", "EGFR", "STK11", "KEAP1", "NFE2L2", "SMARCA4", "TP53", "RB1", "CDKN2A")
for (g in c(genes, "NRF2")) lung[[g]] <- altered_status(data, lung$line, g, config)

genotype_by_histology <- lung %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(c(genes, "NRF2")), names_to = "gene", values_to = "altered") %>%
    filter(!is.na(altered)) %>%
    group_by(gene) %>%
    summarise(
        fisher_p = fisher.test(table(histology, altered), simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 1e4)$p.value,
        Adenocarcinoma = sprintf("%d/%d", sum(altered[histology == "Adenocarcinoma"]), sum(histology == "Adenocarcinoma")),
        Squamous = sprintf("%d/%d", sum(altered[histology == "Squamous"]), sum(histology == "Squamous")),
        Neuroendocrine = sprintf("%d/%d", sum(altered[histology == "Neuroendocrine"]), sum(histology == "Neuroendocrine")),
        `Other NSCLC` = sprintf("%d/%d", sum(altered[histology == "Other NSCLC"]), sum(histology == "Other NSCLC")),
        Other = sprintf("%d/%d", sum(altered[histology == "Other"]), sum(histology == "Other")),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(fisher_p)
genotype_by_histology

# batch vs histology
table(lung$histology, lung$batch)
fisher.test(table(lung$histology, lung$batch), simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 1e4)$p.value
```

```{r genotypes-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
histology_levels <- c("Adenocarcinoma", "Squamous", "Neuroendocrine", "Other NSCLC", "Other")
p <- lung %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(c(genes, "NRF2")), names_to = "gene", values_to = "altered") %>%
    filter(altered %in% TRUE) %>%
    count(gene, histology) %>%
    mutate(histology = factor(histology, levels = histology_levels)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(n, gene, fill = histology)) +
    geom_col() +
    scale_fill_manual(values = uc_palette(histology_levels)) +
    labs(x = "Altered lung lines", y = NULL, fill = NULL, title = "Altered lung lines by histology") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "genotypes_by_histology", output_dir, width = 8, height = 4)
p
```

## 3. Metabolic effect of histology

```{r metabolic}
# PCA of the lung lines: R2 of histology and batch on PC1-5
pc <- prcomp(data$log2[lung$line, ], center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
scores <- as_tibble(pc$x[, 1:5]) %>% mutate(line = lung$line) %>% left_join(lung, by = "line")
sapply(c(histology = "histology", batch = "batch"), function(f)
    sapply(paste0("PC", 1:5), function(k) round(summary(lm(scores[[k]] ~ factor(scores[[f]])))$r.squared, 2)))

# limma F-test of histology, adjusted for batch
X <- model.matrix(~ batch + histology, data = lung)
fit <- limma::eBayes(limma::lmFit(t(data$log2[lung$line, ]), X))
histology_coefs <- grep("^histology", colnames(X))
f_test <- limma::topTable(fit, coef = histology_coefs, number = Inf)
c(ions_adj_p_below_0.05 = sum(f_test$adj.P.Val < 0.05), null_share = round(limma::propTrueNull(f_test$P.Value), 2))
```

```{r pca-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
p <- ggplot(scores, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = factor(histology, levels = histology_levels))) +
    geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = uc_palette(histology_levels)) +
    labs(colour = NULL, title = "PCA of the lung lines by histology") +
    theme_uc()
save_figure(p, "pca_histology", output_dir)
p
```

## 4. Lung contrasts with and without histology

```{r refit}
# the lung contrasts of the analysis, fitted as specified and with histology added
lung_contrasts <- list(
    nrf2_lung = config$differential$contrasts$nrf2_lung,
    stk11_lung = config$differential$contrasts$stk11_lung,
    kras_lung = list(group = "KRAS", tissues = "Lung", covariates = c("TP53", "STK11", "KEAP1"))
)
refit <- bind_rows(lapply(names(lung_contrasts), function(id) {
    # histology is added here explicitly, so the configured blocking is left out
    contrast <- lung_contrasts[[id]]
    contrast$blocking <- NULL
    d <- contrast_lines(data, contrast, config) %>% left_join(select(lung, line, histology), by = "line")
    without <- fit_contrast(data, d, contrast_design(d, contrast$covariates))$table
    with <- fit_contrast(data, d, contrast_design(d, c("histology", contrast$covariates)))$table
    both <- inner_join(select(without, feature_id, name, t_without = t, adj_without = adj.P.Val),
                       select(with, feature_id, t_with = t, adj_with = adj.P.Val), by = "feature_id")
    tibble(
        contrast = id, altered = sum(d$group), unaltered = sum(!d$group),
        adj_p_below_0.05_without = sum(both$adj_without < 0.05),
        adj_p_below_0.05_with = sum(both$adj_with < 0.05),
        spearman_t = cor(both$t_without, both$t_with, method = "spearman"),
        glutathione_adj_p_without = both$adj_without[both$name == "Glutathione"],
        glutathione_adj_p_with = both$adj_with[both$name == "Glutathione"]
    )
}))
as.data.frame(refit)
```


## Interpretation

- **Annotation:** the DepMap Oncotree subtypes agree with the Cellosaurus
  disease text for nearly all lines. The 85 lung lines are 39
  adenocarcinoma, 15 squamous, 14 neuroendocrine (12 small cell, 2
  carcinoid), 15 other non-small cell and 2 other.
- **Several genotypes depend on histology:**
  - RB1 is altered in 9 of 14 neuroendocrine lines;
  - CDKN2A is rarely altered in them (1 of 12);
  - STK11 occurs in adenocarcinoma (14 of 39) but in none of 15 squamous lines.

  KRAS leans towards adenocarcinoma (16/39 vs 2/15 squamous, p = 0.17).
  NRF2 activation does not depend on histology (p = 0.80).
- **Histology is partly confounded with batch:** the neuroendocrine lines
  were all cultured in batches 4–7 (p = 0.008). Since these batches also hold
  other histologies, batch and histology can both enter a model.
- **Histology has a modest metabolic effect:** it explains a quarter of PC4
  and 15 ions differ at adjusted p < 0.05 (batch-adjusted F-test). This is
  less than batch (a third of PC2).
- **Adding histology to the lung contrasts changes little.** The
  t-statistics correlate at 0.91–0.98. The positive control keeps
  glutathione significant (adjusted p 0.005; 17 instead of 25 significant
  ions). STK11 and KRAS remain without significant ions. Histology is
  therefore not the reason for the null results of analysis/06.

**Recommendation:** add histology as a blocking factor to all lung genotype
contrasts (F2, F3, F5). It costs four degrees of freedom and protects the
genes whose frequency depends on histology (RB1, CDKN2A, STK11) from
reflecting histology instead. The histology contrasts (F1) are feasible:
neuroendocrine vs non-small cell 14/69, adenocarcinoma vs squamous 39/15,
with batch in the model.
